BEN Engine — Product and engineering briefingSchreiber AI · what was built, how it is verified, how to run it

01 / 14

BEN Engine, Business Edge Node

All-in-one modular data centers named by IT power: power, cooling, compute and controls in one sealed enclosure, from an outdoor cabinet to a 40 ft liquid-cooled module, with Schreiber AI's controls, twin and commissioning layer. The same system scales to a 2 MW center.

  • Core, the all-in-one box: BEN 5 2–5 kW cabinet · BEN 30 10–30 kW (10 ft) · BEN 150 50–150 kW (20 ft) · BEN 500 150–500 kW (40 ft); capability example: BEN 2000 800–2,000 kW hall
  • Every enclosure NEMA 4X / IP66, hose-tested; hardening H1 / H2 / H3 selectable
  • Modules: Power, Cooling, Compute, Controls; buy one or all
  • Mission profiles set class, redundancy, climate, compliance and the risk list

Speaker notes

Audience: engineers, integrators, facilities leads. Names changed on 2026-11-08: the number is now the IT kW, not the container length (docs/TIER_AND_ENCLOSURE_DECISION.md); old keys still load. Set expectations: every number on these slides comes from code in the repository and the evidence file is docs/VALIDATION.md.

A concrete scenario

A regional clinic wants inference on patient data on-site: healthcare profile, 2N power, A1 class, generator standard.

  • Selector: BEN 150, healthcare, hot/humid climate
  • Output: 480 V service size, UPS kVA, battery kWh under the NFPA 855 threshold, cooling units derated for 38 °C design day
  • Proposal, drawings, compliance pack and risk disclosure generated from that configuration

Speaker notes

Walk the selector live on the product page (web/index.html) or the dashboard. Show the validation error path by setting racks to 1 at 150 kW.

03 / 14

BEN 2000: the single 2 MW center

The capability example, not the lead product. Not a container: a prefabricated, relocatable data hall of three site-joined wide-body modules, a power module and a plant yard.

  • Config: 1,600 kW IT in 48 racks (DLC), 12.47 kV MV service, 2 × 2,500 kVA transformers (2N), 2 × 2,000 kW UPS strings, 3 × 1,250 kW generators (N+1), 7 CDUs, PUE 1.13, 109 t
  • Controls: one PLC per module plus a plant PLC, two edge computers, three border routers, 102 Pods; life safety per module, hardwired
  • A building, not equipment: IBC Group B / F-1 permit, NFPA 855 battery rooms, NFPA 110 Level 1, SPCC, ASHRAE 188 water plan
  • Schedule ≈ 52 weeks: utility MV service (26–52 wk) on the critical path; civil 20 wk, module set 3 days, E15 seal test, E16 transfer test at SAT

Speaker notes

python -m ben_engine.config --tier ben2000 prints these numbers. Twin, CFD per module, drawings (site plan A-000 + per-module sheets) and BOM-ben2000 are generated and run in simulation (docs/VALIDATION.md section 4a); every physical value (module mass, water use, utility lead time, module pricing) is unverified, so say sized and documented, not proven. Built by modular-building manufacturers (MANUFACTURING_STRATEGY.md section 3.2).

04 / 14

Element-proof and hardened

Every BEN starts watertight (NEMA 4X / IP66, hose-tested per UL 50E); two hardening packages sit on top.

  • H1 Standard: IP66 envelope, gasketed and hose-tested penetrations (E14), ISO 12944 C3, climate-package wind and seismic, keyed access and door contacts
  • H2 Severe environment: 600 mm flood plinth, C5-M marine coating and anodes, ePM1 dust filtration, hurricane door hardware, 67 m/s wind; auto-recommended for coastal, desert, arctic and alpine sites
  • H3 Hardened / government: UL 752 ballistic panels (level 3–8), ASTM F3038 forced-entry doors, IK10, mantrap, tamper detection, optional 80 dB HEMP shield (MIL-STD-188-125-1), CMMC controls pack
  • The hose test is in the warranty: repeated every 3 years and after relocation; shield integrity tested annually at H3

Speaker notes

Config.hardening drives the envelope mass adder, catalog cost lines, compliance pack rows (COMPLIANCE.md section 15), maintenance add-ons and the warranty conditions. Say plainly: TEMPEST-ready, not TEMPEST-certified; HEMP shielding is a vendor-certified enclosure plus our IEEE 299 test. The rain-only 3R rating is retired everywhere.

05 / 14

One configuration drives everything

config.py is the base model: sizing rules, validation, presets. Downstream generators consume it.

  • BOM with price-confidence split (bom.py + parts_catalog.json)
  • IFC drawing set with CTQ/CTP tables (design/drawings)
  • Twin, CFD, sweeps, commissioning (software/ben_engine)
  • Dashboard 3-D scene and product page selector (JS port with a parity test)

Speaker notes

Mention the parity test: tests/test_selector_parity.py runs node against the Python model so the website cannot drift from engineering.

06 / 14

The digital twin

Lumped thermal and power-chain model with faults, alarms and sensor specs; fit-able from commissioning data.

  • Faults: cooling unit fail, utility loss, door open, filter clog, leak, sensor drift, generator fail
  • Alarms follow ASHRAE class limits of the profile
  • analysis.py fits recirculation, bypass, thermal mass from a load step and predicts with 95 % intervals

Speaker notes

Caveat: thermal masses are design values until measured. The fitter flags envelope UA as weakly identifiable from indoor data; say so.

07 / 14

CFD for layout, not for absolute numbers

2-D lattice-Boltzmann airflow with heat and tracer transport runs per tier in seconds.

  • BEN 150 grid 232 × 90 at 25 mm, 14.6 s runtime
  • Containment closed and supply > demand: recirculation about 0; fan turn-down to 0.9 or a failed unit: 30–40 % recirculation at the end racks
  • Recirculation profile feeds the twin per rack

Speaker notes

Reynolds number in the lattice is ~70 versus ~1e5 real; it is a relative tool for ranking layouts and scenario deltas. The 3-D CFD is on the roadmap after lighthouse data exists.

08 / 14

Measurement plan and calibration

Sensors chosen for the quantities we predict, with uncertainty budgets, tares and placement effects.

  • Rack inlets at 0.4 / 1.2 / 1.8 m, probes 50 mm off perforated doors
  • Differential pressure tared with fans off; taps away from fan discharge
  • GUM budgets: DS18B20 ±0.17 K, SHT45 ±0.14 K, SDP810 ±0.46 Pa at 12 Pa, 4–20 mA loop ±0.025 mA (computed)

Speaker notes

Two budget claims in PROTOCOL.md were not met by the computed budgets (RH and dP); they are left as findings in docs/ANALYSIS_AND_CALIBRATION.md rather than quietly edited.

09 / 14

Controls: industrial platform, BEN Mesh, hardwired life safety

BEN Controls Pro: Phoenix Contact PLCnext PLC in a UL 508A panel + OnLogic edge computer (TPM). BEN Controls Lite: Revolution Pi for the BEN 5. Both: our BEN Pods on a secure Thread mesh.

  • BEN Pod: Silicon Labs MGM240P with Secure Vault High, per-device certificate, attestation at join, signed firmware; two Pods per rack, no sensor cabling
  • Firmware core: 37 host unit tests pass; telemetry JSON byte-exact to the protocol spec; 1 h ring buffer and failsafe outputs; EFR32 build not run here
  • IEC 62443 zones (PLC 62443-4-1 certified process, TPM measured boot); no internet dependency; PLC watchdog and Pod attestation are commissioning checks

Speaker notes

Be precise: the EFR32/OpenThread HAL has never been compiled against the real SDK and attestation has not run on silicon. The PLC, edge computer and Pods are priced in the BOM (controls +0.3 to +0.9 % of a unit) and not yet bought. Everything platform-independent is tested. Decision record: docs/CONTROLS_HARDWARE_DECISION.md.

10 / 14

Build it with workers who have minimal experience

Assembly instructions in ASD-STE100 with hold points for licensed trades, QC forms and CTQ/CTP references.

  • Receiving → container prep (welder hold point) → envelope → fit-out → electrical (licensed) → cooling (licensed) → controls → fire (certified) → FAT → transport → site → SAT
  • 0 instructions over 20 words; banned-word check passes
  • Concept renders per stage, generated from the configuration

Speaker notes

Renders are labelled concept renders. The interference checks table in design/drawings/INTERFERENCE_CHECKS.md is worth showing to engineers: it is what changed the cooling defaults.

11 / 14

Commissioning: the same script in the factory and on site

Ten steps, pass/fail per step, CSV with SHA-256, signature block; the customer can run it.

  • Sensor sanity, I/O point-to-point, meter vs PDU reconciliation, sequential cooling start and failover, load step, ride-through, alarm verification, export
  • BEN 150 simulation: all 10 pass; ride-through 2.1 min to ASHRAE A2 max, UPS empty at 11.8 min

Speaker notes

Run it live: PYTHONPATH=software python -m ben_engine.commissioning --sim --tier ben150 --yes --out /tmp/r.md. Show the report.

12 / 14

Compliance findings that changed the design

A2L refrigerant charge limits, NFPA 855 at 20 kWh, NEC 110.26 vestibule, container as Group U structure.

  • In-row DX specified with R-513A/R-515B
  • Battery energy capped under 20 kWh on BEN 5/30/150 by default
  • Electrical vestibule on 480 V tiers; second egress door at ≥1000 A frames on BEN 500
  • CSC re-certification after modification; PE-stamped anchorage per climate wind speed
  • BEN 2000 adds building permit, MV service, UL 1558 switchgear, NFPA 855 battery rooms, SPCC and ASHRAE 188 rows; hardening adds UL 50E, UL 752, ASTM F3038, IK10, MIL-STD-188-125-1

Speaker notes

docs/COMPLIANCE.md section 0 lists these with the calculation basis and what could not be verified (NFPA 76 edition, ASHRAE 15/34 2025).

13 / 14

Validation summary

Verified in simulation and on host; unverified on hardware; least accurate items named.

  • Python suite and firmware host tests pass; Playwright e2e exercises the dashboard
  • Unverified: EFR32 Pod build, edge computer image, PLC project, any physical behaviour
  • Least accurate: ride-through minutes, envelope UA, CFD absolutes, estimate-status prices

Speaker notes

Read docs/VALIDATION.md before presenting; update numbers to the latest run.
